title: Confidence interval for population mean with known standard deviation
scenario_markdown: An industrial quality engineer monitors the tensile strength of composite polymer rods. Extensive historical production data establishes that the population standard deviation is known to be $\sigma = 12.0\text{ MPa}$. A random sample of $n = 49$ rods yields a sample mean tensile strength of $\bar{x} = 150.0\text{ MPa}$. Construct and interpret a $95\%$ confidence interval for the true population mean tensile strength $\mu$.
assumptions: Tensile strength follows an approximately normal distribution or CLT applies since n = 49 >= 30
Independent random sample of composite polymer rods
Population standard deviation is known from historical quality controls (sigma = 12.0 MPa), justifying the standard normal Z distribution
source_refs: Course Module 4: Sampling Distribution & Confidence Interval

stages.prompt_markdown: Which critical value distribution and value should be used to construct this $95\%$ confidence interval?

options.hint_markdown: Student's t is required when sigma is unknown and estimated by s. When sigma is known, use the standard normal Z distribution.
$Z^* = 1.645$ corresponds to a $90\%$ confidence interval; for $95\%$, the two-tailed critical value is $Z^* = 1.960$.

stages.explanation_markdown: Because the true population standard deviation $\sigma = 12.0\text{ MPa}$ is known and $n = 49 \ge 30$, the sampling distribution of $\bar{X}$ is normal with standard error $\sigma / \sqrt{n}$. For a $95\%$ confidence level, $\alpha = 0.05$ split evenly across both tails gives $\alpha/2 = 0.025$, yielding critical value $Z^* = 1.960$. Excel formula: `=NORM.S.INV(0.975)`.

stages.prompt_markdown: Calculate the margin of error $E = Z^* \cdot \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}$ for this $95\%$ confidence interval.

options.hint_markdown: Remember that standard error is $\sigma / \sqrt{n} = 12 / \sqrt{49} = 1.7143\text{ MPa}$, not $\sigma$ directly.
Standard error divides by $\sqrt{n} = 7$, not by $n = 49$.

stages.explanation_markdown: The standard error is $SE = \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}} = \frac{12.0}{\sqrt{49}} = \frac{12.0}{7} \approx 1.7143\text{ MPa}$. The margin of error is $E = Z^* \times SE = 1.95996 \times 1.714286 \approx 3.360\text{ MPa}$. In Excel, `=CONFIDENCE.NORM(0.05, 12, 49)` directly computes this margin of error as $3.360$.

stages.prompt_markdown: Determine the resulting $95\%$ confidence interval and identify its valid statistical interpretation.

options.text_markdown: $[146.64, 153.36]\text{ MPa}$: We are $95\%$ confident that the true population mean tensile strength $\mu$ lies between $146.64\text{ MPa}$ and $153.36\text{ MPa}$.
$[146.64, 153.36]\text{ MPa}$: $95\%$ of all individual polymer rods have tensile strength between $146.64\text{ MPa}$ and $153.36\text{ MPa}$.
options.hint_markdown: A confidence interval estimates the unknown population mean parameter $\mu$, not the dispersion of individual observations.
The confidence interval bounds are $\bar{x} \pm E = 150 \pm 3.36$, not $\bar{x} \pm \sigma$.

stages.explanation_markdown: The confidence interval bounds are $\bar{x} \pm E = 150.0 \pm 3.36 = [146.64, 153.36]\text{ MPa}$. Under repeated random sampling of size $49$, $95\%$ of such constructed intervals will enclose the fixed, unknown population parameter $\mu$.
